===
言也三丁擇一分曹角射李抱真蓋嘗行
之山東矣弓箭立社官給田以備其甲馬
蘇軾蓋嘗行之河朔矣邊郡勇悍民樂於
自守而南民近習於兵亦往往有能出力
以自捍乎賊者因而行之不可乎人之言
曰鹽利當興而私販爲難革曾不知公鹽
徼所以私販熾買窩者夥矣而其賣之者
誰歟此之不求而顧彼之禁吾未見其爲
得也然恤竈而後鹽利廣惠商而後鹽法
punctuated:
勝計也？召募不可，復議為召募；調遣不可，復議為調遣，其費又何可勝計也？是故召募調遣不罷，非所以省財；而土著不練，兵不簡，則召募調遣又何可以終罷？然簡兵非愚之言也。二十為兵，六十免為民，在漢固嘗行之矣。不任征戰者減充小分，勝甲者陞大分，在唐固嘗行之矣。稍倣其法而酌之人情，落籍者聽其以親代，而不可者則寧虛其籍，斯不亦可乎？練土著亦非愚言也。三丁擇一，分曹角射，李抱真蓋嘗行之山東矣。弓箭立社，官給田以備其甲馬，蘇軾蓋嘗行之河朔矣。邊郡勇悍，民樂於自守，而南民近習於兵，亦往往有能出力以自捍乎賊者，因而行之，不可乎？
人之言曰：「塩利當興，而私販為難革。」曽不知公塩徵所以私販熾。買窩者姦矣，而其賣之者誰歟？此之不求，而顧彼之禁，吾未見其為得也。然恤竈而後塩利廣，惠商而後塩法
translation_en:
…how could the expense ever be reckoned? When recruitment fails, further recruitment is proposed; when troop dispatches fail, further dispatches are proposed. How, again, could their expense ever be reckoned? Thus, unless recruitment and troop dispatches cease, there is no way to economize. Yet unless local inhabitants are trained and soldiers screened, how can recruitment and dispatches ever cease altogether? Screening soldiers, however, is no invention of this foolish student. Becoming a soldier at twenty and being discharged at sixty to return to civilian status was already practiced under the Han. Reducing those unfit for campaigning to the lesser allotment and promoting those capable of bearing armor to the greater allotment was already practiced under the Tang. Might we not follow these methods to some degree, adapting them to people’s circumstances, allowing those removed from the rolls to provide relatives as substitutes, and, where this is impossible, preferring to leave their places vacant?
Training local inhabitants is likewise no invention of mine. Selecting one man out of every three adult males and dividing them into groups to compete in archery was a practice Li Baozhen had already instituted in Shandong. Organizing archery associations and having the government grant land to provide for their armor and horses was a practice Su Shi had already instituted in Heshuo. The people of the frontier commanderies are brave and fierce, and willingly defend themselves. Southern people, too, have recently become accustomed to warfare, and many can exert themselves to resist bandits. Could we not build upon this and put these measures into effect?
People say, “Revenue from salt should be increased, but private trafficking is difficult to eradicate.” They fail to realize that exactions on government salt [?] are precisely what cause private trafficking to flourish. Those who buy salt-distribution franchises are indeed unscrupulous, but who sells these to them? To neglect investigating the latter and concern oneself instead with prohibiting the former seems to me no sound approach. Yet only by aiding salt producers can salt revenues grow, and only by benefiting merchants can the salt regulations…

title: 嘉靖三十八年會試錄
text:
通引目餘塩不括而後中於邊者衆是不
可以不講矣人之言曰屯田當復而兼併
為難清曾不知北郡多曠而南地之可耕
者亦豈為少歟經略其新而漸圖其舊吾
未見其不可也然更番時而後人情宜遠
近均而後道里便統屬明而後事務舉是
又不可不講矣夫在籍者簡則兵精土著
者練則兵益由之而召募調遣可罷焉是
理兵乃所以理乎財也塩法行而外有所
===
入屯田行而内有所出是理財又所以養
乎兵也簡兵練土著可以舒急於一時而
塩法屯田可以垂利於萬世今日之計宜
無出此者舍此不講將必為桑孔金陵之
策矣嗚呼下以擾民而上不便於公又何
忍於言乎然自兵警以来上之博咨而采
議者非不甚勤也下之畢慮而獻謀者非
不甚詳也而卒莫能效者何耶毋亦虛文
相應而奉行於其下者猶未至焉耳頃者
alt_text:
通引目餘鹽不括而後中於邊者衆是不
可以不講矣人之言曰屯田當復而無併
爲難清曾不知北郡多曠而南地之可耕
者亦豈爲少歟經略其新而漸圖其舊吾
未見其不可也然更番將而後人情宜遠
近均而後道里便統屬明而後事務舉是
又不可不講矣夫在籍者簡則兵精士著
者練則兵益由之而召募調遣可罷焉是
理兵乃所以理乎財也鹽法行而外有所
===
入屯田行而內有所出是理財又所以養
乎兵也簡兵練士著可以舒急於一時而
鹽法屯田可以垂利於萬世今日之計宜
無出此者舍此不講將必爲桑孔金陵之
策矣嗚呼下以擾民而上不便於公又何
忍於言乎然自兵警以來上之悖咨而采
議者非不甚勤也下之畢慮而獻謀者非
不甚詳也而卒莫能效者何耶毋亦虛文
相應而奉行於其下者猶未至焉耳頃者
punctuated:
通；引目餘塩不括，而後中於邊者衆，是不可以不講矣。人之言曰：「屯田當復，而兼併為難清。」曾不知北郡多曠，而南地之可耕者亦豈為少歟？經略其新，而漸圖其舊，吾未見其不可也。然更番時而後人情宜，遠近均而後道里便，統屬明而後事務舉，是又不可不講矣。
夫在籍者簡則兵精，土著者練則兵益，由之而召募調遣可罷焉。是理兵乃所以理乎財也。塩法行而外有所入，屯田行而内有所出，是理財又所以養乎兵也。簡兵練土著，可以舒急於一時；而塩法屯田，可以垂利於萬世。今日之計，宜無出此者。舍此不講，將必為桑孔金陵之策矣。嗚呼！下以擾民，而上不便於公，又何忍於言乎？
然自兵警以来，上之博咨而采議者非不甚勤也，下之畢慮而獻謀者非不甚詳也，而卒莫能效者何耶？毋亦虛文相應，而奉行於其下者猶未至焉耳？頃者
translation_en:
…operate smoothly. Only when surplus salt beyond the quantities covered by salt certificates is not seized will many merchants supply grain at the frontier in exchange for salt rights. These matters must be carefully considered. People say: “Military agricultural colonies ought to be restored, but land engrossment is difficult to eliminate.” They fail to recognize that the northern prefectures contain much vacant land; surely cultivable land in the south is also far from scarce? Develop new holdings and gradually address the old ones: I see no reason why this cannot be done. Yet only with timely rotations will arrangements suit the men; only with an equitable distribution of near and distant assignments will travel be manageable; and only with clear lines of command will affairs be carried out. These matters, too, must be carefully considered.
If those on the military registers are selected, the troops will be of high quality; if local inhabitants are trained, military strength will increase. Recruitment and troop transfers can thereby be discontinued. Thus, managing the military is itself a means of managing finances. When the salt regulations are implemented, revenue will come in from outside; when military agricultural colonies operate, supplies will be produced within. Thus, managing finances is also a means of supporting the military. Selecting troops and training local inhabitants can relieve immediate emergencies, while the salt regulations and military agricultural colonies can confer benefits for countless generations. No plan for the present should surpass these. If we abandon these measures without considering them, we will inevitably resort to the policies of Sang Hongyang, Kong Jin, and the man of Jinling [Wang Anshi]. Alas! Such policies harass the people below and bring no benefit to the public purse above. How could one bear even to propose them?
Yet since military alarms began, those above have been most diligent in consulting widely and gathering proposals, and those below have been most thorough in exhausting their thoughts and offering plans. Why, then, have none ultimately proved effective? Is it perhaps simply that they respond to one another with empty paperwork, while implementation by their subordinates remains inadequate? Recently…

title: 嘉靖三十八年會試錄
text:
皇上特
命諸臣往覈邊儲又閱視南北軍實責使練兵
限之漸不得調遣而屯田盐法則又歲
遣臺臣察之凡當事諸臣震疊
明威之下無不思實効其力者愚見弊漸革而
諸法將無不復矣尚何公私匱乏之足慮
也哉

限之漸不得調遣而屯田塩法則又歲

translation_en: …His Majesty specially commanded the officials to investigate frontier provisions and also to inspect military resources in the north and south, holding them responsible for training troops, imposing graduated limits [?], and prohibiting their redeployment. As for military agricultural colonies and the salt administration, he also sends censorial officials annually to inspect them. All officials responsible for these affairs, awed by his august authority, seek to devote their efforts to producing tangible results. In my humble view, abuses are gradually being corrected, and all these institutions will soon be restored. What further cause, then, is there to worry about shortages in public and private resources?

translation_en:
Postface to the Metropolitan Examination Record

May our sagely emperor enjoy long life and nurture men of talent. This year, siwei [?], is the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign, destined to endure for tens of thousands upon tens of thousands of years. Compared with the four seasons, it is only the beginning of spring. Qian is yang; it represents Heaven and the ruler. Yang arises with the first and flourishes in spring. In the Book of Changes, spring corresponds to Tai, Peace; Tai signifies good fortune and successful passage. Thus clouds move and rain falls, and the myriad things flow into their forms: only then can Qian benefit all under Heaven with its excellent bounty.

Our sagely emperor embodies Qian and acts with vigor, wondrously wielding the virtue of yang to become the people’s ruler and teacher. His voice sets the pitch standard; his person sets the measure. Day by day, scholars are molded and warmed by his influence, and year by year the transforming influence of the Way grows ever more abundant. punctuated: 畿士，于時臣已謂士濟濟矣。今合四海九州之士，統六籍校之，類能仰窺聖皇雲漢昭回之章，而不詭於敬一諸訓旨焉。壽考作人之效，於是大著，蓋益濟濟勝曩矣。此與品物資始於乾元而流形焉者何異？泰所以吉亨歟！夫天道泰，品物遭之，品物之幸；世道泰，士遭之，士之幸。士知虞周乎？上有堯舜文武之君，而八元八凱四友九臣之倫，其榮聲亦彰施到今。何者？聖作類從而附之
translation_en: …candidates of the metropolitan region. Even then, your servant already considered the worthy scholars numerous indeed. Now scholars from all within the Four Seas and the Nine Provinces have been assembled and examined across the Six Classics. They can generally glimpse, with reverence, the sagely emperor’s writings, radiant as the Milky Way, without departing from the purport of his instructions on reverent unity. The efficacy of nurturing men over long years is thus abundantly manifest: worthy scholars are still more numerous than before. How does this differ from the myriad things deriving their beginnings from the primal power of Qian and flowing into their forms? Is this not why Tai, or Peace, brings good fortune and success? When the Way of Heaven is at peace, it is the good fortune of the myriad things to encounter it; when the human world is at peace, it is the good fortune of scholars to encounter it. Do scholars know of the ages of Yu and Zhou? Above were rulers such as Yao, Shun, Wen, and Wu, while the illustrious reputations of men such as the Eight Worthies, the Eight Talented Ones, the Four Friends, and the Nine Ministers have likewise shone down to the present day. Why? When a sage arises, those of his kind follow and attach themselves to him…

title: 嘉靖三十八年會試錄
text:
青雲也士今遭
聖皇當不令虞周士得擅其榮譽
臣誠為士慶之虞周之時固
皆稱泰然在虞洚水滔天黎
民阻饑百姓不親不遜蠻夷
猾夏而冦賊姦宄嘗以咨之
周則昆夷獫狁及殷餘頑之
屬其矯虔尤甚賴虞周君臣
同心迄用底績然亦已勤矣
今天下泰於虞周時矣南交來
庭矣河暫溢而旋就道矣嵗
間告歉頃屢登矣溟島鯨鯢
取而京觀之矣萑澤藪剽者
馘矣細黠誘蠢胡

punctuated: 青雲也。士今遭聖皇，當不令虞周士得擅其榮譽。臣誠為士慶之。虞周之時，固皆稱泰，然在虞，洚水滔天，黎民阻饑，百姓不親，不遜，蠻夷猾夏，而冦賊姦宄，嘗以咨之。周則昆夷、獫狁及殷餘頑之屬，其矯虔尤甚。賴虞周君臣同心，迄用底績，然亦已勤矣。今天下泰於虞周時矣！南交來庭矣，河暫溢而旋就道矣，嵗間告歉，頃屢登矣，溟島鯨鯢取而京觀之矣，萑澤藪剽者馘矣，細黠誘蠢胡
translation_en:
…to the azure clouds. Scholars today have encountered our sage emperor; surely they should not allow the scholars of Yu and Zhou to monopolize such honor and renown. Your servant sincerely congratulates them. The ages of Yu and Zhou were indeed both acclaimed as times of peace and prosperity. Yet under Yu, floodwaters rose to the heavens, the common people suffered hunger, the people lacked affection and obedience, and the Man and Yi peoples threw the Chinese realm into disorder. Marauders, robbers, and evildoers within and without were matters on which the ruler sought counsel. Under Zhou, peoples such as the Kunyi and Xianyun, together with the remaining recalcitrant subjects of Yin, were especially violent and rapacious. Thanks to the unity of purpose between rulers and ministers under Yu and Zhou, their undertakings were finally accomplished; yet this required great toil.
Today the realm enjoys greater peace and prosperity than in the days of Yu and Zhou! Southern Jiao has come to court. The Yellow River briefly overflowed but soon returned to its course. There were reports of poor harvests in some years, but recently abundant harvests have followed one another. The great whales of the ocean islands—the pirate chiefs—have been captured, and their corpses heaped into victory mounds. The plunderers lurking in reed marshes and thickets have been slain. Petty, crafty men entice the benighted Hu …

title: 嘉靖三十八年會試錄
text:
天威褫其魄群兇矣禮樂備矣法
度彰矣聲教訖矣好生之仁
洽矣和氣薰蒸三光全而寒
暑時矣雨風露雷各得其職
矣草木鳥獸咸若矣竒祥上
瑞曼羨煜雪歲荐臻矣士今
所遭不尤幸歟臣誠為士尤
===
慶之臣自辛丑歲應科荷
聖皇親賜教育掄備侍從頃又荷
拔擢今得駿奔
天衢臣所自幸自慶尤倍萬也
乾造罔極戴誠切心然而未知所
以為報竊聞人臣有以人事
君之義今恭至□士之

===
天衢臣所自幸自慶允倍萬也
乾造罔極戴誠切心然而未知所
以爲報竊聞人臣而以人事
君之義今恭奉
punctuated:
天威褫其魄，群兇矣。禮樂備矣，法度彰矣，聲教訖矣，好生之仁洽矣。和氣薰蒸，三光全而寒暑時矣；雨風露雷各得其職矣；草木鳥獸咸若矣；竒祥上瑞，曼羨煜雪，歲荐臻矣。士今所遭，不尤幸歟？臣誠為士尤慶之。
臣自辛丑歲應科，荷聖皇親賜教育，掄備侍從，頃又荷拔擢，今得駿奔天衢。臣所自幸自慶，尤倍萬也。乾造罔極，戴誠切心，然而未知所以為報。竊聞人臣有以人事君之義，今恭至□士之
translation_en:
…Your heavenly might has robbed them of their courage—the assembled villains [?]. Rites and music are complete; laws and institutions are manifest; your civilizing influence has reached everywhere; and your benevolence, cherishing life, has spread throughout. Harmonious influences pervade all things: the sun, moon, and stars shine unimpaired, and cold and heat arrive in their seasons. Rain, wind, dew, and thunder each perform their proper functions. Plants, trees, birds, and beasts all flourish in accord with their nature. Wondrous auspices and supreme portents, abundant and brilliant [?], arrive repeatedly year after year. Are not scholars especially fortunate to encounter such an age? Your servant indeed rejoices particularly on their behalf.
Since sitting the examination in the xinchou year (1541), your servant has received instruction personally bestowed by Your Sagely Majesty and has been selected to serve among your attendants. Recently I have again received promotion, and now I may hasten along the heavenly thoroughfare. My own sense of good fortune and rejoicing is ten thousand times greater still. Your creative bounty, like Heaven’s, knows no bounds; heartfelt gratitude presses upon me, yet I do not know how to repay it. I have humbly heard that a minister has a duty to serve his sovereign by presenting worthy men. Now, respectfully … scholars’ … [?]

punctuated: 命，念可藉以報萬分一者，在得士耳。臣方恭辭于迎和門，未效纖勞，輒先拜珍饌、文綺之賜。恩私益渥，臣用是益矢心得士，冀不仰負任使。入闈來，夙夜與臣璣等矢公矢勤，遵制額錄三百人。夫錄之者，錄其能言道也；而聖訓所謂行如其言，臣未知其若何也。臣聞之，世道貴泰，尤貴恒泰。
translation_en: …the commission, I reflected that only by obtaining worthy men could I repay even one ten-thousandth of Your Majesty’s favor. When I respectfully took my leave at Yinghe Gate, before rendering the slightest service, I had already received gifts of fine foods and patterned silks. Your gracious favor grew still more abundant. I therefore devoted myself all the more firmly to obtaining worthy men, hoping not to fail the trust placed in me. Since entering the examination compound, I have worked day and night with Your servant Ji and the others, pledging impartiality and diligence, and have selected three hundred men in accordance with the prescribed quota. In selecting them, we selected them for their ability to expound the Way. Yet as to whether their conduct matches their words, as Your Majesty’s sacred instruction requires, I do not know how they will measure up. I have heard that peace and prosperity are prized in the affairs of the world, but enduring peace and prosperity are prized still more.

title: 嘉靖三十八年會試錄

治世獲匡佐之良又曰

translation_en:
… The sagely emperor issues commands as circumstances require and adjusts and regulates affairs as is fitting [?], exhausting his care in preserving peace and prosperity. Yet reverently carrying out his will and striving to assist him rests with his ministers. The sagely emperor once prayed to Heaven: “May I obtain worthy men to support and assist me in governing the age.” He also said: “May their assistance in government match the excellence of the Yu and Zhou eras.” His resolve to summon outstanding men and honor the Lord on High is precisely what preserves peace and prosperity. How could those who serve as his ministers bear to fail him?

The second yang line of the hexagram Tai (Peace) attains union with one who follows the central course because of its brilliance and greatness. Thus one must possess the virtue of Tai’s second yang line before one can follow, as a kindred spirit, the fifth yang line of Qian (The Creative), and prove worthy of this meeting of wind and cloud, this intercourse of Heaven and Earth. These scholars are now advancing together, like clumps of thatch pulled up with their intertwined roots, and will soon have their names entered on the rolls of official service. title: 嘉靖三十八年會試錄
text:
士夫
天極奠而嵗功著者二氣五行宣
其化也
皇極奠而治功洽者四鄰九德煕
其績也士既幸遭泰且親見
聖皇切於保泰其尚相與祗承
德心協保無疆而勵翼
===
===
主泰之
聖皇永以祉元吉哉
中順大夫太常寺少卿兼翰
林院學士掌院事嚴訥謹序
alt_text:
士夫
天極參而歲功遂者二氣五行宣
其化也
皇極參而治功洽者四鄰九德熙
其績也士既幸遭泰且親見
聖皇切於保泰其尚相與祇承
德心協保無疆而勵翼
===
主泰之
聖皇永以祉元吉哉
中順大夫太常寺少卿兼翰
林院學士掌院事嚴訥謹序
punctuated:
士夫。
天極奠而嵗功著者，二氣五行宣其化也；皇極奠而治功洽者，四鄰九德煕其績也。士既幸遭泰，且親見聖皇切於保泰，其尚相與祗承德心，協保無疆，而勵翼主泰之聖皇，永以祉元吉哉！
中順大夫、太常寺少卿兼翰林院學士、掌院事嚴訥謹序。
translation_en:
…the scholar-officials.

When Heaven’s ultimate standard is established and the achievements of the seasons become manifest, it is because the two forces of yin and yang and the Five Phases unfold their transforming activity. When the imperial ultimate standard is established and the achievements of government extend everywhere, it is because the ministers on the ruler’s four sides and men possessing the nine virtues bring their accomplishments to fruition. Scholars have been fortunate enough to encounter an age of peace and have themselves witnessed the sage emperor’s earnest concern to preserve it. May they together reverently receive his virtuous intentions, cooperate in preserving this peace without limit, and exert themselves to assist the sage emperor who presides over it, so that he may forever enjoy blessings and supreme good fortune!

Preface respectfully composed by Yan Na, Grand Master of Central Compliance, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy and in charge of the Academy’s affairs.
